newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian central bank revokes Jelgava's license.
newsitem.headline: Latvian central bank revokes Jelgava's license.

text.p: The Bank of Latvia said on Friday that it had revoked the licence of Jelgava bank, one of the smallest banks operating in the Baltic state.
"The Bank of Latvia removed Jelgava Bank's licence today because its equity capital did not reach the one million lats required by law," a Bank of Latvia spokesman told Reuters.
He added that the bank had also failed to meet minimum capital sufficiency and short-term liquidity requirements.
Latvia now has 34 licensed banks, a number most observers consider too high for an emerging economy with only 2.5 million people.

More mergers and licence removals are expected as the central bank tightens its rules to try to prevent a repetition of the crisis which struck the sector last year with the closure of the country's largest bank.
